title: AND–OR formula and game-tree evaluation

problem.name: AND–OR formula and game-tree evaluation
problem.statement_latex:
Given a fixed read-once formula $F$ with $N$ input leaves and gates AND, OR and NOT, query input bits and compute $F(x)$. For alternating AND--OR trees, this decides the winner of a finite perfect-information game with known tree and queried terminal outcomes.
Complexity counts queries to the leaf bits; gate complexity additionally includes access to the preprocessed formula graph.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(\sqrt N)$ queries, quantum-walk and span-program formula evaluation.
quantum.details_latex: The bound applies to fixed read-once AND--OR formulas, allowing negations on inputs. Efficient implementations have nearly matching time after preprocessing the formula. The output is the Boolean value at the root.
quantum.headline_text: $O(\sqrt N)$ queries, quantum-walk and span-program formula evaluation.
quantum.details_text: The bound applies to fixed read-once AND–OR formulas, allowing negations on inputs. Efficient implementations have nearly matching time after preprocessing the formula. The output is the Boolean value at the root.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(N^c)$ for balanced binary trees, randomized alpha--beta pruning, where $c=\log_2((1+\sqrt{33})/4)\approx0.753$.
classical.details_latex: The randomized algorithm evaluates children in random order and stops as soon as the parent value is determined. This is the optimal randomized classical bound for the balanced alternating binary tree. Arbitrary formulas have structure-dependent classical complexity and the general $O(N)$ leaf-reading upper bound.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial: $N^{0.753\ldots}\to N^{1/2}$ on balanced binary trees. The mechanism is a quantum walk or span-program reflection algorithm.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous: the balanced-tree classical and quantum exponents have matching lower bounds.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant evaluation uses logarithmic graph-address registers, phase-estimation ancillas and coherent access to the preprocessed formula. Regular balanced trees admit succinct graph descriptions.
